subject: Publish request: Nimbus Health case study — sensitivity check after support incident
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Draft case study for Nimbus Health — request for sensitivity check

Hi Tessa —

We just received sign-off from Nimbus on a short customer story, but CS flagged a recent support outage that affected a handful of their users in August. They gave conditional approval to publish as long as we: (a) don't cite exact affected user counts, and (b) include a note that recent fixes have been validated in their staging environment.

Draft and incident timeline attached (nimbus-draft-case-study-v2.pdf, incident-timeline.xlsx).

Can you run a sensitivity check and let me know if legal / leadership sign-off is required? I think a short testimonial with redacted numbers might be safe, but want to confirm before we schedule the blog and PR outreach.

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2026-10-01T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft case study for Nimbus Health — request for sensitivity check

Thanks for the heads-up and for attaching the drafts. High level reaction: hold public distribution until we verify the full remediation and get explicit language approval from Nimbus. A couple of asks so we can scope approvals quickly: 

- Marissa: can you paste the Nimbus quote they approved (or forward the exact email) so we can confirm wording?
- Please add a short incident timeline (who saw what and when) in the spreadsheet — which I see you attached, but flag any gaps.
- Legal should review the quote and the proposed redaction; Neha, can you take this?

Vivek, if you have a preference on tone (full case study vs short testimonial) now would be helpful — I want to avoid going to press with anything that could look tone-deaf.

Best,
Tessa
Director, Customer Marketing
Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-10-02T11:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft case study for Nimbus Health — request for sensitivity check

Appreciate the cautious approach. My guidance: no full case study publish for at least 30 days post-incident confirmation in production, and we should require a short executive approval from Nimbus (VP level) for anything referencing the outage or remediation. For a testimonial we can proceed sooner if: (1) all numerical impact is redacted, (2) CS confirms no active churn risk, and (3) marketing includes a brief contextual callout about remediation and current stability.

If Legal (Neha) flags any contractual language, we follow legal's lead. Marissa, please get the VP approval line from Nimbus or ask Sara to loop the VP in writing.

Vivek
VP, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-10-05T15:34:00-07:00
Subject: Decision: publish redacted testimonial, postpone full case study

Thanks everyone — decision below:

1) Publish a short testimonial (1–2 paragraphs) using the redacted draft that Aaron approved. Do not include any numerical counts or revenue impacts. Include the suggested contextual sentence: "a targeted outage affecting a small subset of pilot users was resolved and validated."

2) Postpone the full case study until 30 days after production confirmation and no further incidents; legal (Neha) to review the final redacted testimonial copy before publish.

3) Marissa: proceed to send the redacted draft to Nimbus for final sign-off and request an explicit OK from Aaron in writing once we incorporate any minor copy suggestions. Also add a small in-post footnote that links to a joint post-mortem if Nimbus agrees (optional).

I'll coordinate notification to PR and hold any press outreach until we have Neha's sign-off and the final email from Aaron.

-Tessa
Director, Customer Marketing
Redwood Inference
